bearings.paper_claim: Money-flow network among politically active 501(c) nonprofits and SMLLCs. A tie means funds were exchanged, tie width is dollar amount, and node size is betweenness (Figure 1). The top-ranked organization, Freedom Partners Chamber of Commerce, has out-degree 90 (Table 5). The paper does not state how its network data were built: its background sources are news and IRS material from 2010-2014, and the network comes from earlier unpublished work.
bearings.paper_location: Section 1 p.343-344 (Figure 1 and its description); Section 2 lines 211-216 on the unpublished precursor study; Table 5 p.347
bearings.system_side: Mentat walks FEC-reported committee-to-committee edges breadth-first to depth 3 (reachable_rows default max_depth=3). allocate() spreads each root's funding pro rata over observed outflows and raises an error if root funding is not conserved. Unattributable dollars go to unresolved buckets (depth_limit, cycle, no_observed_outflow). The allocate() docstring calls the result a conditional pro-rata scenario, not traced dollars.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Scope statement only. Money that passes through a non-disclosing nonprofit before reaching a committee is invisible to Mentat's committee graph. The paper gives no data-construction method, so its network cannot validate any edge set. Its network is a single partisan donor network from about 2010-2015. Do not import its ranking as evidence about any industry; any key-node ranking on Mentat's graph is a heuristic output (D-025).
bearings.verifier_note: Code claims confirmed: depth 3, pro-rata conservation, and docstring wording. The claim that the authors built the network from news and IRS sources, not FEC filings, is not in the paper. It never states its data construction, and its reference 13 is a Sunlight piece about FEC quarterly filings. Rewritten to what the text supports.

bearings.paper_claim: Expert-weighted centralities: out-degree 0.50199, total degree 0.14517, eigenvector 0.11045, betweenness 0.07489 (CR 0.062). TOPSIS on this composite matches the plain out-degree order only for the top two of eight. Corner Table LLC (out-degree 7) ranks 3rd and TC4 Trust (out-degree 38) ranks 7th. The authors state that no significant changes resulted, and they validate the composite against no outcome.
bearings.paper_location: Section 2, Tables 2, 4 and 5, p.346-347; Section 5, p.352
bearings.system_side: InfluenceScore = 0.60 x max-normalized weighted out-degree + 0.25 x max-normalized betweenness + 0.15 x max-normalized eigenvector, rescaled to 0-100. The weights are hand-set. Per the record, the score was retired from the Influence pillar (AB13 = 0) but still feeds the underdog lens. The retirement and lens use were not checked against code.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Both composites use judgment weights led by out-degree, so the structural comparison holds. The paper adds a consistency check and a sensitivity sweep but no outcome test, so it cannot justify the 0.60/0.25/0.15 weights or reverse the retirement. Its ties are dollar flows among nonprofits, not cosponsorship. The outcome test that matters is Sotoudeh 2024: does centrality predict bill passage.
bearings.verifier_note: Every paper number in the claim matches Tables 4 and 5 and Section 5. The code weights 0.60, 0.25 and 0.15 and the rescale to 0-100 are confirmed at the cited lines. Retirement status and underdog-lens use were not verified from code.

bearings.paper_claim: Criterion weights come from AHP pairwise comparison on Saaty's nine-point scale, accepted at CR below 0.10 (here 0.062). Robustness follows Alinezhad and Amini Equation 1: change one weight in 0.1 steps, rescale the others proportionally, and track rank. Raising the out-degree weight keeps Freedom Partners Chamber of Commerce first. Raising the weight the paper labels lowest (closeness, Figure 5) lets Center to Protect Patients Rights overtake it.
bearings.paper_location: Section 2, Tables 3-4, p.346-347; Section 3, Equation 1 and Figures 4-5, p.347-348
bearings.system_side: Pillar weights are owner policy, set as constants: Leg 0.45, Press 0.10, Influence 0.40, Demo 0.05. The summary says they are unratified (S-5 open) and that the record conflicts on the ratified set (30/25/40/5 vs 25/30/40/5). Those two statements were not verified.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The one-weight proportional-rescale sweep can be used directly for the open top-133 sensitivity question. AHP would only document owner judgment and check its internal coherence; it gives no outcome validity, and the paper's own weights are unvalidated. Any AHP-derived set must be labelled owner policy with its CR, never an estimate.
bearings.verifier_note: Weights and code location confirmed. The summary's claim that the top-ranked node holds under the sweep is true only for the out-degree sweep. The overtake comes from the closeness sweep. The paper calls closeness the lowest criterion, but Table 4 gives authority (0.03418) the lowest weight and closeness 0.03525. Ratification status not verified.

summary_issues: Summary says the Freedom Partners ranking survives a one-weight sensitivity sweep. Section 3 and Figure 5 show Center to Protect Patients Rights overtaking it when the closeness weight is raised. Only the out-degree sweep leaves it first.
Summary and extract call the TOPSIS output a closeness coefficient (0.754). The paper's Table 5 is labelled larger better and never uses that term. The item's flags repeat the error.

State equalizing mix of about 85 percent non-kinetic is not exactly reproduced. Recomputing from Table 7 gives about 84.6 percent when the DMN cell BC is 0.548, but about 80.2 percent with the text value 0.480645. Table 7 (0.548) and the text (0.480645) conflict on that cell; the item reports only the text value.

Prudential claim is wrong for the DMN. The paper and the item say the DMN plays C always with security level 0.137. In Table 7 the DMN's C security level is 0.091; its maximin strategy is D, at 0.137848. The State's 0.139 level (strategy A) reproduces.

Ten-strategy solution: the printed x4 = 0.8 gives weights summing to 1.72 and a positive objective, so it is not the solution. x4 = 0.08 satisfies the sum constraint and reproduces q = 0.0595 and Z of about -0.0012 with p = 0.084. The item's statement that the solution is internally inconsistent is right, but 0.08 is recoverable from the paper's own constraints. The NLP is a 5-action State by 2-action DMN game, not the 10-strategy list the item describes.
Nash arbitration point (0.31, 0.3192) reproduces approximately (about 0.309, 0.320) on the convex hull of Table 7 with security levels as disagreement point, using the 0.548 DMN cell.

The item's paul_alignment section cites a Paul note on Furnas, a centrality note and a Sotoudeh highlight. The record shows n_annots 0 and paul_entries empty, so these are unsupported by the record and were not verified.

The item's coincidence flag about the legacy workbook (0.80, sums to 1.72, brain file moneyball-workbook-lineage-and-june-audit.md line 61) is outside this paper. It was not checked and should not enter the vault as a bearing on this work.
